newsitem.title: JAPAN: Political jigsaw puzzle likely after Japan's polls.
newsitem.headline: Political jigsaw puzzle likely after Japan's polls.

text.p: Prospects are slim for any party to win an outright majority in the October 20 Japanese general election.
The following are the likely scenarios that could emerge:

LDP WINS MAJORITY: If the Liberal Democratic Party, largest member of the current governing coalition, wins more than 251 of 500 Lower House seats, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto remains in power, provided he wins his home constituency.

If the LDP wins a majority with no more than 260 seats it might seek a renewed alliance with its two small allies Sakigake and the Socialists in order to form a comfortable majority of more than 265 seats. This number gives the ruling coalition chairmanships of all the standing parliamentary committees for smooth passage of legislation.

LDP WINS 230-250 SEATS: The LDP will seek an alliance with the small Sakigake, Socialists, independents and would-be defectors from the opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) to form a majority bloc. Hashimoto will likely stay in power.

LDP WINS 220-229 SEATS: Hashimoto will survive if the LDP successfully cements an alliance with the new Democratic Party under Yukio Hatoyama, plus the Sakigake and Socialists. If the LDP fails to lure the Democrats, the main opposition Shinshinto may have a chance to form a government.

LDP WINS FEWER THAN 220 SEATS: Hashimoto can lose his job and the LDP might seek a so-called "grand alliance" with Shinshinto under LDP strongman Seiroku Kajiyama. If this fails, the LDP could lead a weak, minority government.

SHINSHINTO BECOMES BIGGEST PARTY: If Shinshinto ends up with some 220 seats and becomes the biggest party but short of a majority, leader Ichiro Ozawa would be at the centre of moves to form a non-LDP coalition.

Here again, Hatoyama's Democratic party will hold the key. Besides Ozawa, a likely candidate for prime minister in a Shinshinto-led coalition is ex-premier Morihiro Hosokawa, the reformist who came to power at the head of an anti-LDP alliance in 1993.

DEMOCRATS WIN MORE THAN 100: This will probably mean that the two bigger parties will have no more than 200 seats each, and party leader Yukio Hatoyama or co-leader Naoto Kan, the popular Health Minister who spearheaded a probe into a widespread AIDS scandal, could be offered the prime minister's job by either one of the two big parties. If the Democrats refuse to enter into a coalition with either of the parties, this may increase chances of a grand LDP-Shinshinto alliance.
